label: thm:comparison
statement:
\begin{theorem}[Comparison theorem]\label{thm:comparison}
Let $\mathscr R$ be a recursion category with ranges and binary
restriction coproducts, let $\mathcal A$ be a restriction category with
ranges, restriction zeros, and binary restriction coproducts, and let
$F:\mathscr R\to\mathcal A$ be a range functor.
Choose a Turing morphism $\tau:U\times U\rightharpoonup U$ and an
isomorphism $b:U\to U+U$. Define
\[
 h=b\tau\Delta_U:U\rightharpoonup U+U,\qquad
 a_0=h^*(1_U+0_U),\qquad a_1=h^*(0_U+1_U).
\]
Let $P,N$ be disjoint restriction idempotents on $FU$ such that
$F(a_0)\le P$ and $F(a_1)\le N$. Suppose that
$s:FU\rightharpoonup FU+FU$ satisfies
\[
 s^*(1_{FU}+0_{FU})=N,\qquad
 s^*(0_{FU}+1_{FU})=P,
\]
and that there is a morphism $\ell:U\rightharpoonup U+U$ with
$F\ell=\chi_{U,U}s$.
Then there is a total morphism $g:U\to U$ such that
\[
 (Fg)^*P=(Fg)^*N=0_{FU}.
\]
For any such $g$, if $F(1_U)\ne0$ and inverse image along $Fg$ preserves the join
$P\vee N$, then $P\vee N\ne1_{FU}$.
\end{theorem}
reconstruction: Factor the constant-in-the-first-argument program for the putative lift. Substitution of (id,g) gives hg=ℓg. After the coproduct comparison, pulling back both tags gives equality of the two inverse images bounded by the opposite domains. Their meet is zero. Only the further nonzero-identity and join-preservation hypotheses rule out coverage.

label: cor:separator
statement:
\begin{corollary}[Lifted separators]\label{cor:separator}
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:comparison} on
$\mathscr R$, $\mathcal A$, $F$, $\tau$, and $b$, suppose that
$F(1_U)\ne0$ and inverse images along total morphisms in $\mathcal A$ preserve
binary joins. A complementary pair $P,N$ on $FU$ satisfying
$F(a_0)\le P$ and $F(a_1)\le N$ admits no pair of morphisms
$s:FU\rightharpoonup FU+FU$ and
$\ell:U\rightharpoonup U+U$ with
\[
 s^*(1_{FU}+0_{FU})=N,\qquad
 s^*(0_{FU}+1_{FU})=P,\qquad
 F\ell=\chi_{U,U}s.
\]
\end{corollary}
reconstruction: A complementary target separator satisfying the two diagonal bounds cannot have a swapped conditional together with a source lift when all total inverse images preserve joins and F1 is nonzero.

label: cor:source-conditionals
statement:
\begin{corollary}[Inseparability from complementary conditionals]
\label{cor:source-conditionals}
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:comparison} on
$\mathscr R$, $\mathcal A$, $F$, $\tau$, and $b$, suppose that
$F(1_U)\ne0$ and inverse images along total morphisms in $\mathcal A$ preserve
binary joins of restriction idempotents.
Suppose that, for every complementary pair $c,c'$ on $U$, there
is a total morphism $\ell_c:U\to U+U$ satisfying
\[
 \ell_cc=i_1c,\qquad \ell_cc'=i_0c',
\]
where $i_0,i_1:U\to U+U$ are the coproduct injections.
Then the restriction idempotents $a_0,a_1$ of
Theorem~\ref{thm:comparison} are inseparable in $\mathscr R$.
\end{corollary}
reconstruction: The conditionals need only be supplied in the source for complementary source domains. Full range of the copairing of the domains forces the two partial restrictions of ℓ to recover the opposite tags. Transport along χ then applies the previous result.

label: prop:disjoint-joins
statement:
\begin{proposition}\label{prop:disjoint-joins}
Let $\mathcal C$ be a restriction category with restriction zeros and
binary restriction coproducts. Suppose every pair of parallel morphisms
whose restriction idempotents are disjoint has a join in the restriction
order.
For complementary restriction idempotents $c,c'$ on $X$, the morphism
\[
 \ell_c=(i_1c)\vee(i_0c'):X\rightharpoonup X+X
\]
is total and satisfies $\ell_cc=i_1c$ and $\ell_cc'=i_0c'$.
\end{proposition}
reconstruction: Take the restriction-order join of the two tagged partial identities on complementary supports. Its upper-bound equations supply both branch equations, and its restriction contains their join, hence is total.

label: prop:interpreted-theory
statement:
\begin{proposition}[Interpretation of a sentence theory]\label{prop:interpreted-theory}
Let $F:\mathscr R\to\mathcal A$ be a range functor with split
target, let $\widehat F:\Split(\mathscr R)\to\mathcal A$ be the
extension by chosen splittings, and let $t_A=m_A r_A=\ran(c_{A,S})$
be a sentence theory constructed above. Then
\begin{gather*}
 \widehat F(t_A)=\ran(\widehat F(c_{A,S})),\\
 \widehat F(m_A)\widehat F(r_A)=\widehat F(t_A),\qquad
 \widehat F(r_A)\widehat F(m_A)=1_{\widehat F(T_{A,S})}.
\end{gather*}
Suppose moreover that $\mathcal A=\Par(\mathcal E,\Mono)$ for a
regular category $\mathcal E$. If the total morphism
$\widehat F(c_{A,S})$ factors in $\mathcal E$ through a
monomorphism $v:V\hookrightarrow\widehat F S$, then
there is a unique $h:\widehat F(T_{A,S})\to V$ in $\mathcal E$
such that $v h=\widehat F(m_A)$. Put
\[
 d_V=[\widehat F S\xleftarrow{v}V\xrightarrow{v}\widehat F S]:
 \widehat F S\rightharpoonup\widehat F S.
\]
If $d_V(\widehat F\nu)^*d_V=0$, then
$\widehat F(t_A)(\widehat F\nu)^*\widehat F(t_A)=0$.
\end{proposition}
reconstruction: With a chosen splitting in a split target, the interpreted sentence conclusion has range F̂t and the interpreted maps split it. In Par of a regular category, a total conclusion factoring through V induces a unique factorization of its image through V. Disjoint validity and its negative inverse image imply interpreted consistency.

label: thm:logical-comparison
statement:
\begin{theorem}\label{thm:logical-comparison}
Let $\mathscr R,\mathcal A,F,U,\tau,b,a_0,a_1$ satisfy the
categorical hypotheses and definitions of
Theorem~\ref{thm:comparison}. Suppose that $\mathcal A$ is split,
that inverse images along total morphisms in $\mathcal A$ preserve binary joins
of restriction idempotents, and that $F(1_U)\ne0$.
Let $t_A=\ran(c_{A,S})$ represent a sentence theory in
$\Split(\mathscr R)$ as above, with total negation
$\nu:S\to S$, and let $\theta:(U,1_U)\to S$ be total in
$\Split(\mathscr R)$. With the identity splitting at $1_U$,
$\widehat F\theta:FU\to\widehat F S$. Put
\[
 t=\widehat F(t_A),\qquad
 P=(\widehat F\theta)^*t,\qquad
 N=(\widehat F\theta)^*(\widehat F\nu)^*t.
\]
Assume that $t(\widehat F\nu)^*t=0$, $F(a_0)\le P$, and
$F(a_1)\le N$.
Suppose there are partial morphisms
$s:FU\rightharpoonup FU+FU$ and
$\ell:U\rightharpoonup U+U$ satisfying
\[
 s^*(1_{FU}+0_{FU})=N,\qquad
 s^*(0_{FU}+1_{FU})=P,\qquad
 F\ell=\chi_{U,U}s.
\]
Then there is a total $g:U\to U$ in $\mathscr R$ such that
\[
 (\widehat F(\theta g))^*t=0,\qquad
 (\widehat F(\theta g))^*(\widehat F\nu)^*t=0.
\]
In particular,
\[
 t\vee(\widehat F\nu)^*t\ne1_{\widehat F S},\qquad
 t_A\vee\nu^*t_A\ne1_S.
\]
\end{theorem}
reconstruction: Use the interpreted sentence map to pull the theorem and negative theorem domains back to FU. Interpreted consistency, both reduction bounds and the lifted swapped conditional give a total source g avoiding both. Total inverse image preserving joins gives incompleteness there, and F̂ preserving the source cover gives incompleteness in the source.

label: cor:domain-incompleteness
statement:
\begin{corollary}\label{cor:domain-incompleteness}
Let $\mathcal C$ be a restriction category with restriction zeros and
binary joins of restriction idempotents preserved by inverse image along total morphisms.
Let $a,b$ be inseparable restriction idempotents on $U$. Suppose that
$\theta:U\to S$ and $\nu:S\to S$ are total, and that a restriction
idempotent $t_0$ on $S$ satisfies $a\le\theta^*t_0$ and
$b\le\theta^*\nu^*t_0$.
For every restriction idempotent $t\ge t_0$ on $S$ with $t\,\nu^*t=0_S$,
the pair $t,\nu^*t$ is inseparable. In particular,
$t\vee\nu^*t\ne1_S$.
\end{corollary}
reconstruction: For separated signed bounds at t₀, inseparability of their source pair makes the domains t,ν*t inseparable for each disjoint t≥t₀. The inverse images of any complementary separator along total θ would separate the given domains. No faithful interpretation or global element is required.

label: thm:first-order-reflection
statement:
\begin{theorem}[Generation reflection]\label{thm:first-order-reflection}
Under the preceding hypotheses, $\operatorname{Gen}$ is extensive,
monotone, and idempotent. It is left adjoint to the inclusion
$\iota:\operatorname{Th}_{\mathcal D}(S)\hookrightarrow
\operatorname{Sub}_{\mathcal D}(S)$. Thus, for every axiom
subobject $A$ and sentence theory $T$,
\[
 \operatorname{Gen}(A)\leq T\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A\leq T.
\]
For each theory $T$ choose a representative $i_T:|T|\hookrightarrow S$.
Let $J:\operatorname{Th}_{\mathcal D}(S)\to\mathcal D/S$ send $T$
to $i_T$ and $T\leq U$ to the unique factorization of $i_T$ through $i_U$. Then
$\Gamma(a:A\to S)=\operatorname{Gen}(\im a)$ defines a functor
$\Gamma:\mathcal D/S\to\operatorname{Th}_{\mathcal D}(S)$ with
$\Gamma\dashv J$.
\end{theorem}
reconstruction: Gen is extensive by leaves and monotone by leastness. The formula closure already contains the generated sentences, proving idempotence. Thus Gen is left adjoint to inclusion of closed sentence subobjects. On the slice the left adjoint factors through the regular image, with uniquely determined morphisms to monic theory presentations.

label: thm:translation-galois
statement:
\begin{theorem}[Translation Galois connection]\label{thm:translation-galois}
Let $\sigma:P\to Q$ be a logical translation between presentations
satisfying the hypotheses of
Theorem~\ref{thm:first-order-reflection}. Inverse image along
$\sigma_S$ sends sentence theories to sentence theories, and
\[
 \sigma_\#:\operatorname{Th}_P\rightleftarrows
 \operatorname{Th}_Q:\sigma^*,\qquad
 \sigma_\#(T)=\operatorname{Gen}_Q(\sigma_!T),\qquad
 \sigma_\#\dashv\sigma^*.
\]
Here $\sigma_!$ and $\sigma^*$ abbreviate the image and inverse-image
operations for $\sigma_S$. Moreover,
\[
 \operatorname{Gen}_Q\sigma_!
   =\sigma_\#\operatorname{Gen}_P.
\]
For composable logical translations $\sigma:P\to Q$ and
$\rho:Q\to R$,
\[
 (\rho\sigma)_\#=\rho_\#\sigma_\#,\qquad
 (\rho\sigma)^*=\sigma^*\rho^*.
\]
\end{theorem}
reconstruction: Translate rules with their ordered premise and conclusion maps. Pullback of a closed formula object is rule-closed, hence sentence pullback preserves theories. Compose direct image with generation to obtain its left adjoint; monotonicity gives the natural generation identity and composable translations give the two composition laws.

label: prop:deduction-comparison
statement:
\begin{proposition}[Comparison of deduction]\label{prop:deduction-comparison}
With these data, suppose that for every $A\hookrightarrow S_1$
there is a total morphism
\[
 p_A:GP_{A,S_1}\to P_{L(A),S_2},\qquad
 c_{L(A),S_2}p_A=\sigma Gc_{A,S_1}.
\]
Then $L^{\mathrm{th}}(T)=\operatorname{Gen}_2L(T)$ defines a
functor on theory orders satisfying
\[
 L^{\mathrm{th}}\operatorname{Gen}_1=\operatorname{Gen}_2L,
 \qquad \Gamma_2K=L^{\mathrm{th}}\Gamma_1.
\]
Consequently the left-adjoint square in
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large,row sep=large]
 \mathcal D_1/S_1\arrow[r,"K"]
   \arrow[d,shift right=.8ex,"\Gamma_1"'] &
 \mathcal D_2/S_2\arrow[d,shift right=.8ex,"\Gamma_2"']\\
 \operatorname{Th}_1\arrow[r,"L^{\mathrm{th}}"']
   \arrow[u,shift right=.8ex,"J_1"'] &
 \operatorname{Th}_2\arrow[u,shift right=.8ex,"J_2"']
\end{tikzcd}
\qquad \Gamma_i\dashv J_i
\]
commutes. Factorization through the generated theory gives a natural
transformation $KJ_1\to J_2L^{\mathrm{th}}$.
If $L\dashv R$ on subobject orders, $R$ sends theories to theories
and $L^{\mathrm{th}}\dashv R|_{\operatorname{Th}_2}$.
\end{proposition}
reconstruction: For a regular total functor and sentence comparison, a conclusion-preserving map of sentence derivations for every axiom object induces L(Gen A)≤Gen(LA), the commuting square of left adjoints and the natural comparison into the monic presentation. A right adjoint to L on subobjects restricts to closed objects. The displayed comparison is a hypothesis, with a separate sufficient construction by transposition of an inference comparison.

label: thm:free-first-order-adjunction
statement:
\begin{theorem}[Free first-order adjunction]
\label{thm:free-first-order-adjunction}
Let $\mathcal D=\Tot(\mathscr S)$ be regular with disjoint,
pullback-stable finite coproducts, where $\mathscr S$ is a split
restriction category and every monomorphism of $\mathcal D$ has a partial
inverse in $\mathscr S$. Fix a decidable variable object $V$. For every
$X\in\mathcal D$, assume that $P_X$ has the syntax and variable-list
algebras of Definition~\ref{def:categorical-syntax}, initial in every
parameter slice, and an initial derivation algebra for each axiom
subobject. In $\mathsf{FO}_V(\mathcal D)$, each presentation $P$
has an initial derivation algebra for every $A\hookrightarrow S_P$,
and $T$ in an object $(P,T)$ is a consistent sentence theory of $P$.
Then
\[
 \Sigma_{\mathrm{FO}}:
 \mathsf{Pair}_c(\mathcal D)\rightleftarrows
 \mathsf{FO}_V(\mathcal D):J_{\mathrm{FO}},\qquad
 \Sigma_{\mathrm{FO}}\dashv J_{\mathrm{FO}}.
\]
The unit at $(X,a,b)$ has underlying morphism $\theta_X:X\to S_X$.
The counit $\Sigma_{\mathrm{FO}}J_{\mathrm{FO}}(P,T)\to(P,T)$
is the translation extending $1_{S_P}:S_P\to S_P$.
\end{theorem}
reconstruction: For each disjoint pair whose signed theory is consistent and consistent target presentation on the same decidable variable object, maps X→S_P respecting the positive and negative bounds correspond naturally to syntax translations. Free syntax and list initiality give the unique interpretation. Preservation of occurrences, failure/success substitution and rule instances passes it to theories. Pull the target theory back along evaluation of sentence-indexed atoms to prove the right adjoint lands in the stated pair category. Unit is θ; counit evaluates predicates at themselves.

label: cor:signed-first-order-incompleteness
statement:
\begin{corollary}\label{cor:signed-first-order-incompleteness}
Under the hypotheses of
Theorem~\ref{thm:free-first-order-adjunction}, let $a,b$ be
disjoint subobjects of $X$ and suppose $T_{a,b}$ is consistent.
Then $T_{a,b}$ is essentially incomplete if and only if $(a,b)$
is inseparable in $\mathscr S$, that is, if and only if no complementary
subobjects $C,D$ of $X$ satisfy $a\leq C$ and $b\leq D$.
\end{corollary}
reconstruction: Assume internal consistency of the generated theory. A complete consistent closed extension separates the original pair by pulling back theorem and refutation objects. Conversely a complementary separator is a Boolean assignment. The singleton model makes equality true and quantification the identity on truth values. Induction shows successful substitution preserves evaluation, so the true sentences form a complete consistent closed extension.

label: lem:partial-slice-turing
statement:
\begin{lemma}[Turing structure in partial slices]
\label{lem:partial-slice-turing}
Under these assumptions, $\mathscr C$ and every $\mathscr C[T]$ are
Turing categories. If $Q$ is the original Turing object, with
$\tau:Q\times Q\rightharpoonup Q$, the Turing object in $\mathscr C[T]$
is $T\times Q\to T$. Under the product identification
$(T\times Q)\times_T(T\times Q)\cong T\times(Q\times Q)$, its
Turing morphism is
$1_T\times\tau:T\times(Q\times Q)\rightharpoonup T\times Q$ over $T$.
Let $\mathscr R[T]$ be the full restriction subcategory on the objects
$T\times X\to T$ for $X\in\mathscr R$. Then $\mathscr R[T]$ is a
recursion category and
\[
 \Split(\mathscr R[T])\simeq\mathscr C[T].
\]
\end{lemma}
reconstruction: Split the domain of an arbitrary map to obtain the restriction terminal equation. Extend source parameters to split objects by restricting a total parameter to the split domain. For any X→T, embed its graph into T×Q. In the partial slice the second component determines the computation with its given base projection and common domain. Constant families are isotypical, prodominical and full, and splitting their graph idempotents recovers all slice objects.

label: thm:theory-extension
statement:
\begin{theorem}[Theory extensions and associated categories]
\label{thm:theory-extension}
Let $\mathscr R,\mathscr C,\mathcal D$ and the deductive system
satisfy the preceding assumptions. For internal theories
$t:T\hookrightarrow S$ and $u:U\hookrightarrow S$, let
$i:T\hookrightarrow U$ satisfy $t=ui$. Postcomposition defines a
fully faithful restriction functor
\[
 \Sigma_i:\mathscr C[T]\longrightarrow\mathscr C[U].
\]
Pullback defines $i^*:\mathscr C[U]\to\mathscr C[T]$, and the
underlying categories have adjunctions
\[
 \Sigma_i\dashv i^*\dashv\Sigma_i.
\]
If $i$ is proper, $\Sigma_i$ is not essentially surjective.
For composable theory inclusions $i,j$,
$\Sigma_j\Sigma_i=\Sigma_{ji}$.

The sentence and theorem comparison morphisms in $\mathcal D/U$
are $i\times1_S$ and $i\times i$. They give the commutative square
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
 \Sigma_i(T\times T\to T)
   \arrow[r,"i\times i"]\arrow[d,hook,"\Sigma_i\widetilde t"'] &
 (U\times U\to U)\arrow[d,hook,"\widetilde u"]\\
 \Sigma_i\widetilde S_T\arrow[r,"i\times1_S"'] & \widetilde S_U.
\end{tikzcd}
\]
Equivalently, $\widetilde S_T\cong i^*\widetilde S_U$ and
$\widetilde t\leq i^*\widetilde u$.
\end{theorem}
reconstruction: For a mono i:T→U over sentences, postcompose the span legs' structure maps. Monicity gives full faithfulness. Factor the right leg or the left leg through the pullback to obtain the two inverse hom-set bijections with i*. For a proper i the terminal object over U cannot lie in the image, since an isomorphism would split i. The comparisons on sentences and theorems are i×1 and i×i and postcomposition is strictly functorial.

label: thm:associated-incompleteness
statement:
\begin{theorem}[Incompleteness in an associated category]
\label{thm:associated-incompleteness}
Under the categorical and syntax hypotheses of
Theorem~\ref{thm:theory-extension}, suppose that a logical theorem $\lambda:1\to S$ factors through each
consistent internal sentence theory $u:U\hookrightarrow S$, and write
$\lambda_U:1\to U$ for its factorization. Then for every such $u$,
$u$ is essentially incomplete in $\mathscr C$ if and only if $\widetilde u=B_U(u)$ is
essentially incomplete in $\mathscr C[U]$. Moreover,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 u\text{ is incomplete}
 &\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \widetilde\delta_u\text{ is not total},\\
 (u,\nu^*u)\text{ is inseparable in }\mathscr C
 &\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \widetilde\delta_u\text{ has no total extension in }\mathscr C[U].
\end{aligned}
\]
If a consistent theory $t:T\hookrightarrow S$ admits a total reduction
of an inseparable pair to its theorem and refutation subobjects, every
consistent extension $u\geq t$ has an essentially incomplete theory
$\widetilde u$ in its associated category. The partial morphism $\widetilde\delta_u$ has no total extension.
\end{theorem}
reconstruction: Assume initial derivations in parameter slices and a chosen logical theorem through each consistent theory u. Constant family and evaluation at its theorem point preserve closure via the initial derivation object, finite limits, images and coproducts. A possibly nonconstant complete consistent extension specializes to one in the base. The reflected partial Boolean test is total exactly for a complete theory and has a total extension exactly when the theorem/refutation pair is separable; reductions persist for all consistent extensions.

label: lem:arithmetized-evaluation
statement:
\begin{lemma}\label{lem:arithmetized-evaluation}
For this computation coding, there are an index $u\in\N$ and
primitive-recursive functions
$\operatorname{s},\operatorname{comp}:\N^2\to\N$
such that PA proves functionality
of $G$ and the universal closures of
\begin{align}
 G_u(\langle e,x\rangle,y)
   &\leftrightarrow G(e,x,y),
   \label{eq:arithmetized-universal}\\
 G(\operatorname{s}(e,a),x,y)
   &\leftrightarrow G(e,\langle a,x\rangle,y),
   \label{eq:arithmetized-specialization}\\
 G(\operatorname{comp}(f,e),x,z)
   &\leftrightarrow
     \exists y\,\bigl(G(e,x,y)\land G(f,y,z)\bigr).
   \label{eq:composition}
\end{align}
Regard $u$ as an element of $\mathcal I(\omega\times\omega,\omega)$.
For each fixed $e\in\N$, there is an index
$k_e\in\N$ for which PA proves
\[
 \forall a\forall p\,
 \bigl(G_{k_e}(a,p)\leftrightarrow
       p=\operatorname{s}(\bar e,a)\bigr).
\]
In particular, PA proves $\forall a\exists!p\,G_{k_e}(a,p)$.
\end{lemma}
reconstruction: PA proves functionality for the least successful stage. Translate between the program and categorical pairing conventions to obtain universal interpretation and specialization by primitive recursive s. Dovetailed bounded witness-pair search for sequential computations yields a composition compiler with the PA graph equivalence. Each fixed program has a PA-provably total parameter compiler k_e.

label: lem:syntactic-functional-search
statement:
\begin{lemma}\label{lem:syntactic-functional-search}
For every $\Sigma_1$ formula $\Gamma(x,y)$ there is an index
$a_\Gamma$ such that PA proves
\begin{gather*}
 \forall x\forall y\,
   \bigl(G_{a_\Gamma}(x,y)\longrightarrow\Gamma(x,y)\bigr),\\
 \forall x\,
   \bigl(\exists y\,G_{a_\Gamma}(x,y)
          \longleftrightarrow\exists y\,\Gamma(x,y)\bigr).
\end{gather*}
If $T$ proves that $\Gamma$ is functional, then
\[
 T\vdash\forall x\forall y\,
       \bigl(G_{a_\Gamma}(x,y)\longleftrightarrow\Gamma(x,y)\bigr).
\]
\end{lemma}
reconstruction: A Σ₁ relation has a first-witness search returning some output on exactly its existential domain, provably in PA. A theory proving uniqueness of outputs proves equivalence of the program graph with the given relation. This does not require PA to establish that uniqueness for an arbitrary relation.

label: lem:syntactic-total-category
statement:
\begin{lemma}\label{lem:syntactic-total-category}
There is an equivalence $\mathcal P_T\simeq\mathcal B_T$.
The category $\mathcal B_T$ is regular, with finite coproducts
that are disjoint and stable under pullback. Every monomorphism
of $\mathcal B_T$ has a partial inverse in $\Split(S_T)$.
For $\Gamma:C\to D$ in the predicate presentation, its regular
image is represented by the inclusion
\[
 R_\Gamma(y)\equiv\exists x\,\Gamma(x,y)
 \quad\hookrightarrow\quad D(y).
\]
In particular, every subobject of a predicate $D$ is isomorphic
over $D$ to an inclusion of a $\Sigma_1$ predicate.
\end{lemma}
reconstruction: Represent split total maps by provably total supported functional Σ₁ graphs. Coding isomorphisms give essential surjectivity. Build finite limits by pairing/equalities. Search for antecedents of provable surjections to split regular epis; all maps factor through existential image. Coproducts use parity and inverse-image partitions. Monicity implies provable injectivity from the kernel pair, and the transpose yields a partial inverse and monic subobject presentation.

label: lem:st-finite-sigma1
statement:
\begin{lemma}[Finite membership conditions]
\label{lem:st-finite-sigma1}
Let $C(x)$ be $\Sigma_1$, and let $a$ code a finite sequence with
entries $a_i$. The assertion that all entries satisfy $C$ is equivalent
in $\PA$ to a $\Sigma_1$ formula. Let $m$ be a positive integer and let
$D_0(x),\ldots,D_{m-1}(x)$ be $\Sigma_1$ formulas. Fix a $\Sigma_1$
graph formula $L(x,w)$ for a primitive-recursive program whose values on
$\N$ lie in $\{0,\ldots,m-1\}$. Define the entry condition
\[
 C_L(x)\equiv\bigvee_{j=0}^{m-1}\bigl(L(x,\bar j)\land D_j(x)\bigr).
\]
The assertion that all entries satisfy $C_L$ is also equivalent in $\PA$
to a $\Sigma_1$ formula.
\end{lemma}
reconstruction: Bounded conjunction along a coded list of a Σ₁ predicate admits one list of witnesses by PA induction. Finite disjunction over a fixed finite list of colored predicates yields the designated entry test even if range behavior of the label program is assumed only in the standard model.

label: prop:st-syntax-initiality
statement:
\begin{proposition}[Syntax initiality with parameters]
\label{prop:st-syntax-initiality}
Let $d$ be a nonnegative integer and let $V,\Sigma_k,\Pi_k$ be
objects of $\mathcal B_T$ for $0\leq k\leq d$. Powers below
denote finite products. The endofunctor
$K:\mathcal B_T^2\to\mathcal B_T^2$ defined by
\[
 K(X,Y)=\left(
 V+\coprod_{k=0}^{d}\Sigma_k\times X^k,
 X^2+\coprod_{k=0}^{d}\Pi_k\times X^k+Y+Y^2+V\times Y
 \right)
\]
has an initial algebra in $\mathcal B_T^2$, with carriers
$\Tm$ and $\Fm$. This algebra is stable
under parameters in the sense of Appendix~\ref{app:syntax-theories}: for every object $P$,
its pullback to $(\mathcal B_T/P)^2$ is initial for $K_P$.
\end{proposition}
reconstruction: For bounded arities and arbitrary Σ₁ coefficient objects in the total syntactic category, two-sorted postorder tree syntax is initial over every parameter P. A finite evaluation list of operation traces gives the graph of the fold. Its totality over P and uniqueness follow by PA induction using the algebra carrier and projection equations in T.

label: prop:st-list-initiality
reconstruction: For each carrier V, finite codes whose entries belong to V form the list algebra. Nil and cons decompose uniquely. Evaluate from the last entry over an arbitrary base fiber; induction on length proves provable totality, functionality and uniqueness.

label: prop:st-substitution-realization
statement:
\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:st-substitution-realization}
On the preceding codes, the list operations, free-variable morphisms,
term substitution, and the formula-substitution morphism with codomain
$1+\Fm$ of Appendix~\ref{app:syntax-theories} are represented by algorithms whose
defining equations and preservation of the specified carriers are
provable in $\PA$. Restricting each graph to its source predicate
gives a morphism of $\mathcal B_T$. These are the morphisms
constructed there by parameterized initiality. In particular, the
subobject $\Adm$ is the free-for substitution domain on
these named-variable codes, represented by a complemented
subobject in $\mathcal B_T$.
\end{proposition}
reconstruction: Occurrence lists count repetitions. At ∀y, x=y bypasses substitution in the body. Otherwise reject capture, requiring the recursively substituted body to succeed. Numerical traversals are primitive recursive without signature membership, PA verifies preservation on admissible carriers, and parameterized initiality identifies the traversals with the categorical maps. Success and failure partition the product domain.

label: lem:syntactic-derivation-initiality
statement:
\begin{lemma}\label{lem:syntactic-derivation-initiality}
Let $T\supseteq\PA$, let $F$ be an object of $\mathcal B_T$, and
fix morphisms
\[
 p_n:R_n\longrightarrow F^n,\qquad
 q_n:R_n\longrightarrow F\qquad(0\leq n\leq N),
\]
where $N$ is a fixed nonnegative integer.
The inference endofunctor $H$ of
Appendix~\ref{app:closed-subobjects} has an initial algebra in
$\mathcal B_T/F$.  Its underlying object and conclusion morphism
are represented by $\Sigma_1$ formulas.
\end{lemma}
reconstruction: For arbitrary finite rule objects/morphisms over F, code trees with strict descent to children. A Σ₁ condition checks node labels and matching conclusion/premise codes. A graph for the root gives a total conclusion. Evaluation in any algebra uses a finite trace/value list. Induction in T gives a unique total algebra morphism over F, even when the coefficients use arbitrary Σ₁ representatives.

label: thm:syntactic-generated-theory
statement:
\begin{theorem}\label{thm:syntactic-generated-theory}
Let $T$ be a consistent extension of $\PA$ and put
$\mathcal B_T=\Tot(\Split(S_T))$. Fix a nonnegative integer $d$
and variable and signature objects $V,\Sigma_k,\Pi_k$ of
$\mathcal B_T$ for $0\leq k\leq d$.
The syntax, list, and substitution constructions above realize
the first-order structure of Appendix~\ref{app:syntax-theories}
in $\mathcal B_T$. For every axiom subobject $i_A:A\hookrightarrow S$
of its sentence object, the inference endofunctor $H_A$ has an
initial algebra with conclusion morphism $c_A:P_A\to\Fm$.
Its image is the least subobject of $\Fm$ containing the logical
and nonlogical axioms and closed under generalization and modus
ponens. The sentence pullback of this image is the least sentence
theory containing $A$.

Use the sentence predicate above, and choose the derivation
predicate $P_A(p)$ and conclusion index $e_A$ furnished by the
construction. Put $\operatorname{Th}_A(z)\equiv\exists p\,G_{e_A}(p,z)$.
Then the restriction idempotent
\[
 t_A=[\operatorname{Sent}(z)\land\operatorname{Th}_A(z)]_T:
                  \omega\rightharpoonup\omega
\]
belongs to $S_T$, and its splitting represents that sentence theory.
\end{theorem}
reconstruction: Realize all seven logical schemes and both positive-arity rules for any bounded signature. The initial derivation algebra has least closed formula image; its restriction to the empty-occurrence fiber is the least sentence theory. The sentence-and-provability predicate in the unsplit category ranges through the desired splitting. A c.e. arithmetic presentation supplies its own Σ₁ predicate.

label: prop:model
reconstruction: For each M⊨T, decode numerical graph formulas using the bijections on products and coproducts in M. T-provable uniform equality permits passage to classes. Existential intermediate codes range over all M and give relational composition and actual image. Restriction, zero, products, coproducts, ranges and finite domain joins are preserved.

label: lem:switch
statement:
\begin{lemma}\label{lem:switch}
Let $c,c'$ be complementary restriction idempotents on $X$ in $S_T$.
There is a total morphism $s:X\to X+X$ with
\[
 sc=i_1c,\qquad sc'=i_0c'.
\]
For every $M\models T$, the morphism $\chi_{X,X}^{-1}F_Ms$ is the
unique section of $\nabla_{F_MX}(F_Mc'+F_Mc)$, where
$\chi_{X,X}:F_MX+F_MX\to F_M(X+X)$ is the coproduct isomorphism.
\end{lemma}
reconstruction: A complementary source pair is presented by T-provably disjoint covering Σ₁ predicates. Search the tagged disjunction to obtain a T-provably total morphism, whose interpreted graph is the unique section of the indicated restricted codiagonal in every model.

label: cor:model-pair
statement:
\begin{corollary}\label{cor:model-pair}
For every $M\models T$, the functor $F_M$ satisfies the hypotheses of
Corollary~\ref{cor:source-conditionals}. Thus, for a Turing morphism
$\tau:\omega\times\omega\rightharpoonup\omega$ and an isomorphism
$b:\omega\to\omega+\omega$ in $S_T$, the restriction idempotents
\[
 (b\tau\Delta_\omega)^*(1_\omega+0_\omega),\qquad
 (b\tau\Delta_\omega)^*(0_\omega+1_\omega)
\]
are inseparable in $S_T$.
\end{corollary}
reconstruction: Take any model, any Turing morphism and any coproduct isomorphism of the stated types. Set inverse images preserve joins, M is nonempty and the switch lemma supplies the needed lifts. The source diagonal domains are inseparable.

label: prop:model-total-regular
reconstruction: Interpret each Σ₁ object as its solution set. Terminal, product, equalizer, tagged sum, empty predicate and existential image formulas realize the respective Set constructions, giving preservation of finite limits, coproducts and regular images.

label: lem:semantic-substitution
statement:
\begin{lemma}[Semantic substitution]\label{lem:semantic-substitution}
Let $\sigma:\N\to |K|$ be an assignment of values to variables.
For $x\in\N$ and $a\in|K|$, write
$\sigma[x\mapsto a]:\N\to|K|$ for the assignment obtained
by changing the value of $x$ to $a$. For finite terms $r,t$,
\[
 \llbracket r[x:=t]\rrbracket^K_\sigma
 =\llbracket r\rrbracket^K_{
          \sigma[x\mapsto\llbracket t\rrbracket^K_\sigma]}.
\]
For a finite formula $\varphi$, if
$(\ulcorner\varphi\urcorner,x,\ulcorner t\urcorner)$ lies in
the image of $a_{\N}$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:semantic-substitution}
 K,\sigma\models\varphi[x:=t]
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 K,\sigma[x\mapsto\llbracket t\rrbracket^K_\sigma]
             \models\varphi.
\end{equation}
The substitution morphisms of
Proposition~\ref{prop:st-substitution-realization}, interpreted by
$G_{\N}$, give the codes of $r[x:=t]$ and, when admissible,
$\varphi[x:=t]$.
\end{lemma}
reconstruction: Use induction on finite standard terms and formulas under assignments into a nonempty model of the c.e. axioms. For a different binder, either x is absent or the binder is absent in the replacement term, so assignment updates commute on the relevant body. This identifies truth after successful substitution and the code output of the realized operations.

label: prop:standard-code-soundness
statement:
\begin{proposition}[Soundness on standard codes]
\label{prop:standard-code-soundness}
Let $\Gamma$ be a computably enumerable set of arithmetic sentences,
with axiom subobject $i_A:A\hookrightarrow S$ in
$\mathcal B_{\PA}$, and let $K\models\Gamma$.
There is a unique function
\[
 e_K:G_{\N}P_{A,S}\longrightarrow \operatorname{Th}(K)
 \quad\text{such that}\quad
 \iota_K e_K=G_{\N}c_{A,S}.
\]
If $\nu:S\to S$ is sentence negation, then the subobjects
$\iota_K$ and $(G_{\N}\nu)^*\iota_K$ of $G_{\N}S$ have empty
intersection.
\end{proposition}
reconstruction: Every finite standard derivation in the c.e. presentation is valid in K. Check seven schemes (including both equality substitutions), modus ponens and generalization at every assignment. Unique factorization of sentence conclusion through the truth set follows from monicity, and classical negation gives disjoint inverse image.

label: lem:ultrapower-regular
reconstruction: In Set with choice and a proper ultrafilter on a nonempty index set, coordinate powers preserve terminal and empty sets and products. Fill coordinates off a large set of agreement to witness equalizers and sums; surjections split, so their ultrapowers are surjective. Hence regular images are preserved.

label: lem:ultrapower-comparison
statement:
\begin{lemma}[Comparison with the arithmetic ultrapower]
\label{lem:ultrapower-comparison}
There is a natural isomorphism of functors
\[
 \eta:\mathscr U G_{\N}\xRightarrow{\ \cong\ }G_M:
             \mathcal B_{\PA}\longrightarrow\mathbf{Set}.
\]
On a predicate object $J_{\PA}(C)$ it is the map
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ultrapower-predicate-comparison}
 \eta_{J_{\PA}(C)}:
 \mathscr U(C(\N))\longrightarrow C(M),
 \qquad [c_i]\longmapsto[c_i].
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}
reconstruction: Łoś turns a representative in a predicate object into a point of its interpretation. Fill coordinates outside its large satisfaction set to prove surjectivity. Apply Łoś to the function graph for naturality and transport along a predicate-object presentation.

label: thm:ultrapower-soundness
statement:
\begin{theorem}[Soundness in the arithmetic ultrapower]
\label{thm:ultrapower-soundness}
Let $i_A:A\hookrightarrow S$ and $K$ satisfy the hypotheses of
Proposition~\ref{prop:standard-code-soundness}, and let
$\nu:S\to S$ be syntactic negation in $\mathcal B_{\PA}$.
Let $I$ be nonempty,
let $\mathcal U$ be a proper ultrafilter on $I$, and put
$M=\N^I/\mathcal U$. Define
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \iota_{K,\mathcal U}
   &=\eta_S\mathscr U(\iota_K):\mathscr U(\operatorname{Th}(K))\hookrightarrow G_MS,\\
 e_{K,\mathcal U}
   &=\mathscr U(e_K)\eta_{P_{A,S}}^{-1}:
       G_MP_{A,S}\longrightarrow \mathscr U(\operatorname{Th}(K)).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ultrapower-soundness-factorization}
 \iota_{K,\mathcal U}e_{K,\mathcal U}=G_Mc_{A,S},
\end{equation}
and $\iota_{K,\mathcal U}$ has empty intersection with its inverse
image along $G_M\nu$. Consequently the interpreted theorem
subobject and its inverse image along $G_M\nu$ have empty
intersection. Equivalently, for the restriction idempotent
$t_A=\ran(c_{A,S})$ in $\Split(S_{\PA})$,
\[
 \widehat F_M(t_A)\,
       (\widehat F_M\nu)^*\widehat F_M(t_A)=0.
\]
\end{theorem}
reconstruction: Apply Set ultrapower to the standard soundness factorization, conjugating by η on sentence and proof objects. Finite-limit and empty-set preservation transport the disjointness of validity and its negative. Interpreted theorem domain is contained in transported validity. This does not assume a satisfaction predicate for arbitrary nonstandard formulas.

label: lem:arithmetic-diagonal-representation
statement:
\begin{lemma}[Representation of the diagonal restriction idempotents]
\label{lem:arithmetic-diagonal-representation}
There is a total morphism
$\theta:\omega\to S$ in $\mathcal B_{\PA}$ such that
$(G_{\N}\theta)(n)=\ulcorner\alpha(\bar n)\urcorner$.
Suppose that every axiom of PA is derivable from the c.e.\
sentence set $\Gamma$. For every $M\equiv\N$, the following
inequalities hold in $\Pfn$:
\begin{align*}
 F_M(a_0)&\le
   (\widehat F_M\theta)^*\widehat F_M(t_\Gamma),\\
 F_M(a_1)&\le
   (\widehat F_M\theta)^*(\widehat F_M\nu)^*
                   \widehat F_M(t_\Gamma).
\end{align*}
\end{lemma}
reconstruction: Use the recursive sentence-code map θ(n)=code(α(n̄)), with α,β the even/odd diagonal result. PA proves trace functionality and can verify each standard positive computation and their disjointness. Any c.e. Γ deriving PA proves the corresponding positive/negative numeral instances. The resulting two universal statements hold in ℕ and hence in every elementary equivalent M.

label: lem:arithmetic-proof-search
statement:
\begin{lemma}[A lift constructed by proof search]
\label{lem:arithmetic-proof-search}
For every c.e.\ sentence set $\Gamma$, there is a morphism
$\ell_\Gamma:\omega\rightharpoonup\omega+\omega$ in
$S_{\PA}$ with the following property. In any $M\models\PA$
for which
\[
 C(x)=\operatorname{Prov}_\Gamma(\Theta(x)),\qquad
 C'(x)=\operatorname{Prov}_\Gamma(\operatorname{Neg}(\Theta(x)))
\]
have disjoint truth sets, the partial function
\[
 s_\Gamma=\chi_{\omega,\omega}^{-1}F_M(\ell_\Gamma):
       F_M\omega\rightharpoonup F_M\omega+F_M\omega
\]
in $\Pfn$ satisfies
\[
 s_\Gamma^*(1_{F_M\omega}+0_{F_M\omega})=[C'(M)],\qquad
 s_\Gamma^*(0_{F_M\omega}+1_{F_M\omega})=[C(M)].
\]
Here $[C(M)]$ denotes the partial identity on
$\{x\in M:M\models C(x)\}$, and $[C'(M)]$ is defined in the
same way.
\end{lemma}
reconstruction: One Σ₁ tagged witness search in the fixed S_PA yields ℓΓ for each presentation. Its domain is the disjunction provably in PA. In any model in which the two predicates are disjoint its graph equals the intended relation, proving exactly the swapped tag preimages; no PA proof of Γ's consistency is needed.

label: thm:arithmetic-internal-comparison
statement:
\begin{theorem}[Incompleteness of an internal arithmetic theory]
\label{thm:arithmetic-internal-comparison}
Let $\Gamma$ be a consistent c.e.\ set of arithmetic sentences
from which every PA-axiom is derivable. Its sentence theory
$t_\Gamma$ in $\Split(S_{\PA})$ is incomplete.
Its interpretations under $\widehat F_{\N}$ and under every
$\widehat F_M$, where $M=\N^I/\mathcal U$ for a proper ultrafilter
$\mathcal U$ on a nonempty set $I$, are incomplete.
For the standard interpretation, there is a total morphism
$g:\omega\to\omega$ in $S_{\PA}$ such that, writing
$\gamma=F_{\N}(g):\N\to\N$, every sentence
$\alpha(\overline{\gamma(n)})$ is undecidable from $\Gamma$.
\end{theorem}
reconstruction: For consistent c.e. Γ deriving PA, completeness supplies a model K of Γ. Keep K separate from the code model ℕ or its ultrapower. Soundness in K, the two diagonal bounds, and the search lift instantiate the logical comparison, giving incompleteness internally and in all these interpretations. At ℕ each θ(g(n)) is independent.

label: cor:arithmetic
reconstruction: A recursive separator of the theorem and refutation codes pulls back along Θ to one of the even/odd diagonal. The conditional on this recursive separator has a source program, contradicting the lifted-separator result. A complete consistent c.e. extension of a c.e. extension would decide its theorem side on the recursive set of sentences by simultaneous search.

label: prop:arithmetic-theory-fibers
statement:
\begin{proposition}[Fibers of the derivation family]
\label{prop:arithmetic-theory-fibers}
For every $e\in\N$, the pullback of $c^{\mathrm{all}}$ along
$k_e^{\Fm}$ is the underlying conclusion morphism of an initial
$H_{A_{\Gamma_e}}$-algebra in $\mathcal B/\Fm$.
There is an induced morphism $\iota_e:P_{\Gamma_e}\to P$
in $\mathcal B$, and the square
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
 P_{\Gamma_e}\arrow[r,"\iota_e"]
       \arrow[d,"c_{\Gamma_e}"'] & P\arrow[d,"c"]\\
 S\arrow[r,"k_e^S"'] & E\times S
\end{tikzcd}
\]
is a pullback in $\mathcal B$. Consequently
$(k_e^S)^*m$ is the sentence theory generated by $A_{\Gamma_e}$.
\end{proposition}
reconstruction: Construct one axiom predicate Ax(e,z)=Sent(z)∧(PAax(z)∨W(e,z)); all rules retain e. The numeral singleton is complemented. Splitting off that factor identifies the inference algebra category with a product, hence its first component is an initial algebra for that e. Pullback and regular-image stability give the commutative square on sentence conclusions and its generated theory.

label: thm:uniform-independent-sentences
statement:
\begin{theorem}[Uniform independent sentences]
\label{thm:uniform-independent-sentences}
Let $E=(\omega,1_\omega)$ and let $S$ be the arithmetic sentence
object in $\mathcal B=\Tot(\Split(S_{\PA}))$. For each $e\in\N$,
let $\Gamma_e$ consist of the chosen PA axioms and all arithmetic
sentences on whose codes program $e$ halts. There is a morphism
$q:E\to S$ in $\mathcal B$ such that, for every $e\in\N$ with
$\Gamma_e$ consistent, the
sentence with code $(G_{\N}q)(e)$ is neither provable nor
refutable from $\Gamma_e$.
\end{theorem}
reconstruction: Use the single Σ₁ search on (e,x) and a single total parameter g representing its untagged computation. Diagonal substitution gives h g=ℓ⟨1,g⟩. At a consistent e the two searches are disjoint. Either proof at x=g(e) would put the diagonal in the opposite side whose sign has a PA proof. Thus the same morphism q=θg supplies a sentence independent for each consistent input index.

label: prop:numerical-structure
statement:
\begin{proposition}\label{prop:numerical-structure}
There is an equivalence
\[
 \operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{Split}(\mathrm{Rec}))
       \simeq\mathcal C_{\mathrm{rec}}.
\]
The category $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{rec}}$ is regular, with finite
coproducts that are disjoint and stable under pullback. Under the
displayed equivalence, every monomorphism of $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{rec}}$
corresponds to a restriction monomorphism in
$\operatorname{Split}(\mathrm{Rec})$, and
\[
 \operatorname{Par}(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{rec}},\operatorname{Mono})
       \simeq\operatorname{Split}(\mathrm{Rec}).
\]
\end{proposition}
reconstruction: Use recursive tuple encoding and decoding for the equivalence with c.e. carriers, with the empty tuple handled separately. Finite limits, stable sums and images have their Set carriers, and an injective total map has a partial recursive inverse by search. Coding the two legs' common graph/domain extends the equivalence to partial maps in both directions.

label: prop:arithmetic-theory-realization
reconstruction: Over c.e. carriers and bounded recursive signatures, finite code evaluation using the given partial recursive algebra maps is total on the legal carrier in every parameter slice. Occurrence and substitution folds coincide with the numerical algorithms, and derivation trees with c.e. premises/axiom parameters likewise admit the unique fold over their conclusions.

label: lem:arithmetic-signed-theory
reconstruction: Assume PA consistent. The diagonal pair stays inseparable in the split syntactic category. In the nullary-predicate language, any two opposite derivations admit one finite list of all their positive labels; PA verifies by induction that every leaf and step is true for that one valuation. No global recursive separator is needed. This gives internal consistency, then essential incompleteness.

label: cor:arithmetic-associated-categories
statement:
\begin{corollary}[Arithmetic instance of the extension theorem]
\label{cor:arithmetic-associated-categories}
Assume that $\PA$ is consistent. Let
$u:U\hookrightarrow S^{\pm}$ be any consistent internal sentence
theory containing $t_{\pm}$, and write $t_{\pm}=ui$.
Then
\[
 \Sigma_i:
 \Par(\mathcal B_{\PA}/T_{\pm})
 \longrightarrow
 \Par(\mathcal B_{\PA}/U)
\]
is fully faithful, and is not essentially surjective when $i$ is
proper. Both categories are split Turing categories, and the
theory
\[
 1_U\times u:U\times U\hookrightarrow U\times S^{\pm}
\]
in the latter category is essentially incomplete. Its partial
Boolean morphism, true on the theorem domain and false on the
refutation domain, has no total extension.

Let $\mathscr R_{\PA}[U]$ be the full restriction subcategory of
$\Par(\mathcal B_{\PA}/U)$ on the objects
$U\times X\to U$, for $X$ in $S_{\PA}$.
It is a recursion category, with
$\Split(\mathscr R_{\PA}[U])\simeq\Par(\mathcal B_{\PA}/U)$.
The functor
\[
 S_{\PA}\longrightarrow\mathscr R_{\PA}[U],\qquad
 X\longmapsto(U\times X\to U),\qquad
 f\longmapsto1_U\times f
\]
is faithful and sends $\tau_{\PA}$ to $1_U\times\tau_{\PA}$,
a Turing morphism in $\mathscr R_{\PA}[U]$.
\end{corollary}
reconstruction: For any internal consistent extension of the signed nullary theory, regularity and syntax/derivation initiality in each parameter slice hold, the logical sentence ∀x(x=x) gives a point, and the diagonal reduces. Thus the partial slices have the stated Turing structure, fully faithful inclusion, proper-image obstruction, and the constant extension has no complete consistent enlargement or total Boolean extension.

label: lem:miller-unanimity
statement:
\begin{lemma}\label{lem:miller-unanimity}
There is one oracle program which, from $p\in P_z$ and numerical inputs
$e,n$, computes the partial function $\tau_z:\N^2\rightharpoonup\N$
defined by
\[
 \tau_z(e,n)=m
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 (\forall q\in P_z)\;\Phi_e^q(n)\mathord\downarrow=m.
\]
Its value and its domain of definition depend only on $z$, not on the
chosen binary representation $p$.
\end{lemma}
reconstruction: From any binary name of z one can enumerate the complement of its compact fiber by finite cylinder-image boxes. A finite cylinder subcover decides each successful search for unanimity of one output on the fiber. Dovetail over outputs and use the nonempty fiber for functionality. This gives an actual common partial evaluator, including identical domains across names.

label: prop:miller-category
reconstruction: For uniformly represented partial functions the image search returns the searched value regardless of witness. For injective functions inverse search returns the unique argument. Singletons detect equality, compatible joins run in parallel, and specialization with uniform unanimity gives τ_a total parameter maps. Coding makes the objects isotypical.

label: lem:miller-cut-reduction
reconstruction: For each diagonal index, use distances to finite unions of dyadic boxes missing successful outputs, with the empty-set case fixed to one. An effectively convergent weighted series gives nonnegative computable functions positive on the disjoint even/odd halting opens. A signed affine combination crosses 1/2 exactly there. The Miller property at the specialized program index gives the two *equalities* of preimages.

label: cor:miller-cuts-inseparable
reconstruction: Pulling a uniform separator back along h would separate the uniform diagonal, impossible. Every single binary name computes a possibly different separator using its initial digit, with freedom at 1/2. Thus fixed-oracle interpretation need not send τ_a to a Turing morphism.

label: prop:miller-theory-realization
statement:
\begin{proposition}\label{prop:miller-theory-realization}
The category $\mathcal D_a$ is regular, with finite coproducts that
are disjoint and stable under pullback. Every monomorphism of
$\mathcal D_a$ has a partial inverse in
$\operatorname{Split}(\mathcal E_a)$, and there is a restriction equivalence
\[
 \operatorname{Par}(\mathcal D_a,\operatorname{Mono})
       \simeq\operatorname{Split}(\mathcal E_a).
\]
For $V=\N$ and a recursive signature of bounded finite arity, the
syntax and list algebras of Definition~\ref{def:categorical-syntax}
exist in $\mathcal D_a$ and are stable under parameters.
For every axiom subobject of the sentence object, the inference
endofunctor of Theorem~\ref{thm:first-order-theory} has an initial
algebra of finite derivations.
\end{proposition}
reconstruction: In the split uniform-oracle category, finite limits/effective coproducts and images are computed on carriers. Descent of a function along a surjection has a unique output independent of the representation, though a chosen preimage may depend on it. Monos have partial inverses. Finite recursive signatures admit the required slice syntax folds and finite derivation objects for all semidecidable axiom subobjects.

label: lem:miller-parameterized-deduction
statement:
\begin{lemma}\label{lem:miller-parameterized-deduction}
Let $X$ be an object of $\mathcal D_a$. The first-order language
with variables $\N$, equality, and a nullary predicate for each
label in $X$ has the syntax and list algebras of
Definition~\ref{def:categorical-syntax}, stable under parameters.
For this language and for every recursive signature covered by
Proposition~\ref{prop:miller-theory-realization}, finite derivation
algebras are also stable under parameters. More precisely, if $P$
is an object of $\mathcal D_a$, $\mathsf{Fm}$ is the formula object,
$S$ is the sentence object, and
$A\hookrightarrow P\times S$ is an axiom subobject over $P$, the
corresponding inference endofunctor on
$\mathcal D_a/(P\times\mathsf{Fm})$ has an initial algebra.
\end{lemma}
reconstruction: Arbitrary semidecidable nullary label carriers are allowed because a finite tree makes only finitely many label tests. For those languages and the recursive field signature, keep w fixed at every rule and semidecide every (w,φ) axiom leaf. Evaluation over an arbitrary algebra is uniform in the binary name and unique by tree induction.

label: thm:miller-incompleteness
statement:
\begin{theorem}\label{thm:miller-incompleteness}
Let $a$ be a Miller sequence with property~\eqref{eq:miller-property}.
In the language of ordered fields with constants $c_n$ for $n\in\N$,
let $T_a$ be the deductive closure of the axioms for real closed
ordered fields together with the rational bounds in~\eqref{eq:miller-theory}.
For every consistent extension of $T_a$ in the same language with
an $\mathcal E_a$-semidecidable axiom set, the partial identities on its
theorem and refutation sets are inseparable in
$\operatorname{Split}(\mathcal E_a)$.
In particular, every such extension is incomplete.
\end{theorem}
reconstruction: The real field expanded by the coordinates satisfies all strict bounds. Uniformly semidecide a rational strict bound from successive prefix intervals. In any consistent extension with such an axiom set, n↦code(2c_n<1) sends the left cut to theorems and the right cut to refutations by strict-order asymmetry. Pullback therefore proves inseparability and an independent sentence.

label: cor:miller-associated-categories
statement:
\begin{corollary}\label{cor:miller-associated-categories}
Let $a$ be a Miller sequence, and let $u:U\hookrightarrow S$ be a
consistent internal sentence theory extending $t_a$. The category
\[
 \mathscr C_a[U]=\Par(\mathcal D_a/U,\Mono)
\]
is a Turing category, and its internal theory
\[
 1_U\times u:U\times U\hookrightarrow U\times S
\]
is essentially incomplete. Its theorem and refutation domains are
inseparable. Let $\delta_u:S\rightharpoonup\Two$ be the partial
morphism with domain $u\vee\nu^*u$ taking the value true on $u$
and false on $\nu^*u$. Then
$1_U\times\delta_u:U\times S\rightharpoonup U\times\Two$
has no total extension in $\mathscr C_a[U]$.

If $u':U'\hookrightarrow S$ is another consistent internal
sentence theory and $u=u'i$ for $i:U\hookrightarrow U'$, then
postcomposition induces a fully faithful restriction functor
\[
 \Sigma_i:\mathscr C_a[U]\longrightarrow\mathscr C_a[U'].
\]
This functor is not essentially surjective when $i$ is proper.
\end{corollary}
reconstruction: Each consistent closed extension of the coordinate-bounds theory in the uniform total category is itself available as a semidecidable axiom object. Reflect it and arbitrary parameter-dependent extensions at the global sentence 0=0. The constant theory is essentially incomplete with inseparable domains and no total Boolean extension. Inclusions between such theories give fully faithful partial-slice functors, with proper case outside their essential image.

label: prop:endpoint
statement:
\begin{proposition}\label{prop:endpoint}
The covariant functors $E_j$ preserve restrictions, zeros, ranges,
binary restriction products and coproducts, and finite joins of
restriction idempotents.
For $i=1,2$, the Turing morphism
$\tau:V\times V\rightharpoonup V$ constructed in
Theorem~\ref{thm:fork-turing} is sent
to a Turing morphism on $\N^2$ in $\mathcal K$.
\end{proposition}
reconstruction: Evaluation at any of the three objects preserves the partial-map operations, ranges, finite joins, products and coproducts componentwise. At either endpoint ordinary s-m-n for arbitrary c.e. parameter carriers exhibits total parameters z↦(0,s(z)). The corresponding central evaluator is constrained by the two structure maps.

label: prop:fork-syntax-initial
reconstruction: For V-labelled propositional trees, evaluation in an algebra at each of the three components terminates. Induction using naturality of the algebra shows compatibility with relabelling along both transitions, and the constructor equations force the evaluation.

label: prop:fork-proof-initial
reconstruction: The leaf and modus ponens tree algebra over S is initial. Applying a target algebra to each leaf or compatible pair of child values preserves the conclusion by its slice equation. Naturality at leaves and branching and induction prove the unique fold in the diagram category.

label: thm:fork-proof-presentation
reconstruction: The image of the conclusion is the least c.e. subfunctor closed under the three schemes, two signed axiom families and modus ponens. Positive/negative single-node derivations give the bounds. At each component jointly collect positive labels in two allegedly contradictory proofs; one valuation satisfies both trees and forbids opposite conclusions.

label: thm:cosheaf-observation
statement:
\begin{theorem}\label{thm:cosheaf-observation}
Fix $i\in\{1,2\}$. Let $T\subseteq S$ be a compatible family of
consistent c.e.\ theory extensions as above, and let
$t_T:S\rightharpoonup S$ be its partial identity. The total morphism $E_i\theta$ induces the function
$\theta_i:|V_i|=\N^2\to |S_i|$ on carriers. Define
\[
 P_{i,T}=\{x\in\N^2:\theta_i(x)\in T_i\},\qquad
 N_{i,T}=\{x\in\N^2:\nu_i(\theta_i(x))\in T_i\}.
\]
The restriction idempotents $t_T,\nu^*t_T$ are inseparable in $\mathcal A$.
The sets $P_{i,T},N_{i,T}$ are disjoint c.e.\ subsets of $\N^2$ satisfying
$A_i\subseteq P_{i,T}$ and $B_i\subseteq N_{i,T}$.
They are recursively inseparable. The assignment
$T\mapsto(\omega\times\omega,P_{i,T},N_{i,T})$,
with the identity of $\omega\times\omega$ for extension inclusions, is a
covariant functor from the poset of these families, ordered by componentwise
inclusion, to $\operatorname{Pair}(\mathrm{Rec})$.
The theory with theorem set $T_i$ is incomplete.
\end{theorem}
reconstruction: For compatible consistent c.e. extensions, the signed inequalities give global inseparability. At each endpoint the atom map pulls back the c.e. theorem/refutation sets to disjoint supersets of its recursively inseparable pair. Such sets cannot cover the endpoint. The identity maps give functoriality in theory extension and an undecided atom exists.

label: cor:cosheaf-essential-incompleteness
reconstruction: Given a single consistent c.e.-axiomatized endpoint extension, take its deductive closure there and the original theory at each other component. The family is compatible because both transitions travel to endpoints. Apply the endpoint result.

label: prop:fork-first-order-realization
reconstruction: Use the constant natural-number object for variables and any diagram D for nullary predicate labels. Every finite tree has finitely many c.e. membership tests. Relabelling preserves variables, the capture test, all seven schemes and both rules. Parameter-dependent derivations and arbitrary target algebra folds retain their parameter, giving stable initiality.

label: prop:fork-first-order-conservative
statement:
\begin{proposition}\label{prop:fork-first-order-conservative}
The theory $T_{\mathrm f}$ is consistent and essentially
incomplete in $\mathcal A$. Its restriction to the propositional
language is $T_{\mathrm p}$, that is,
\[
 j^*T_{\mathrm f}=T_{\mathrm p}.
\]
At either endpoint $i=1,2$, every consistent extension of
$(T_{\mathrm f})_i$ in its first-order language with a c.e.\ axiom set
is incomplete.
\end{proposition}
reconstruction: Choose a global atom to define a propositional theorem top. Erase quantifiers, send all equalities to top, and retain the propositional constructors. This retraction commutes with successful substitutions, sends the four extra schemes to explicit propositional theorems and preserves both rules. Hence the first-order theory restricts exactly to the propositional one and is consistent. A complete consistent extension would separate the signed labels. A complete endpoint extension restricts to one propositionally.

label: cor:fork-associated-theories
statement:
\begin{corollary}\label{cor:fork-associated-theories}
Let $t:T_{\mathrm f}\hookrightarrow S_{\mathrm f}$ be the
first-order theory above, and let
$u:U\hookrightarrow S_{\mathrm f}$ be any consistent internal
sentence theory with $t=ui$ for a monomorphism
$i:T_{\mathrm f}\hookrightarrow U$. Then
\[
 \mathcal A[T_{\mathrm f}]=\Par(\mathcal E/T_{\mathrm f},\Mono),
 \qquad
 \mathcal A[U]=\Par(\mathcal E/U,\Mono)
\]
are Turing categories, and postcomposition gives the fully
faithful functor
\[
 \Sigma_i:\mathcal A[T_{\mathrm f}]\longrightarrow\mathcal A[U]
\]
of Theorem~\ref{thm:theory-extension}. It is not essentially
surjective when $i$ is not an isomorphism. The theory
\[
 1_U\times u:U\times U\hookrightarrow U\times S_{\mathrm f}
\]
is essentially incomplete in $\mathcal A[U]$. Its theorem and
refutation domains are inseparable there.
\end{corollary}
reconstruction: In the regular extensive diagram category, parameterized derivation algebras exist and the global propositional tautology survives in every extension. For any consistent inclusion, the partial slices are Turing and the induced fully faithful functor has a proper-image obstruction. Pulling a proposed separator back at this tautology excludes it in the base.

label: def:categorical-syntax
reconstruction: Specify an initial two-sorted term/formula algebra and an initial list algebra for the given variable object, each remaining initial over every parameter object. Terms retain variable names and formulas include equality, negation, implication and a named binder. This is actual structure when assumed.

label: def:sentence-object
reconstruction: Take the inverse image of the empty variable-occurrence list under the formula fold. Equality of occurrence lists is stronger than equality of underlying finite sets, with repetitions kept. Negation restricts to sentences.

label: prop:categorical-substitution
statement:
\begin{proposition}\label{prop:categorical-substitution}
Parameterized initiality uniquely determines morphisms
$a_T:\Tm\times E\to\Tm$ and
$b_F:\Fm\times E\to O(\Fm)$.
Admissibility and formula substitution are defined by the pullback
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
 \Adm\arrow[r,"a_F"]\arrow[d,hook,"i_{\Adm}"'] &
 \Fm\arrow[d,hook,"\ok_{\Fm}"]\\
 \Fm\times E\arrow[r,"b_F"'] & O(\Fm).
\end{tikzcd}
\]
The monomorphism $i_{\Adm}$ is complemented.
\end{proposition}
reconstruction: Fold over (variable,replacement) into pairs recording the original subtree and result. The first projection is the identity by initiality. Terms always succeed; formulas return either failure or success. Pullback of the success summand gives the complemented admissible domain and the substitution morphism.

label: def:deductively-closed
statement:
\begin{definition}\label{def:deductively-closed}
A subobject $m:T\hookrightarrow F$ is closed under these rules if
there is a morphism $\alpha:\coprod_nB_n(T,m)\to T$ with
$m\alpha=\kappa_m$. Equivalently, $(T,m)$ admits an $H$-algebra
structure in $\mathcal D/F$. When $F$ and the rule morphisms specify
a logical calculus, such a subobject is a deductively closed theory
of formulas for that calculus.
\end{definition}
reconstruction: For a finite list of premise/conclusion morphisms a subobject of F is closed when it carries an algebra for the induced inference functor over F. Monicity means the algebra is unique if it exists.

label: thm:least-theorem-subobject
reconstruction: The finite-arity inference functor preserves regular epis by products, base change and finite coproducts. Factor the initial conclusion into regular epi followed by mono. The induced diagonal from the kernel-pair coequalizer makes the image closed; initiality then factors it through every closed subobject.

label: thm:first-order-theory
reconstruction: Specialize this result to seven typed axiom schemes, with admissibility for universal instantiation and both equality substitutions and the fresh-variable test for distribution, plus generalization and modus ponens. Pulling the conclusion to the sentence object pulls the regular image back, giving the sentence part.

label: lem:range-regular-image
statement:
\begin{lemma}[Regular images and ranges]\label{lem:range-regular-image}
Let $\mathcal S$ be a restriction category with ranges in which every
restriction idempotent splits. Suppose $\mathcal D=\Tot(\mathcal S)$
is regular, and let $f:X\to Y$ have regular-image factorization
$f=me$ in $\mathcal D$, with $e:X\twoheadrightarrow I$ and
$m:I\hookrightarrow Y$.
If $m$ has a partial inverse $r:Y\rightharpoonup I$ in $\mathcal S$,
then $\ran(f)=mr=\bar r$.
\end{lemma}
reconstruction: For any total f=me in split restriction structure with regular totals, suppose the image mono has partial inverse r. Then mr fixes f; any other restriction idempotent fixing f splits through a mono through which f factors totally. The image factors through that mono and gives mr below it, proving ran f=mr.

label: prop:fork-cosheaves
statement:
\begin{proposition}\label{prop:fork-cosheaves}
Restriction to $O_0,O_1,O_2$ defines an equivalence
$\operatorname{CoSh}(X,\mathbf{Set})\simeq\mathbf{Set}^{J}$,
where $J=(1\leftarrow0\to2)$. A quasi-inverse sends a diagram
$Y_1\xleftarrow{r_1^Y}Y_0\xrightarrow{r_2^Y}Y_2$ to the cosheaf
with value $Y_j$ at $O_j$ and $Y_1\amalg_{Y_0}Y_2$ at $X$.
\end{proposition}
reconstruction: All covers of proper nonempty opens contain them. The only independent gluing condition is the pushout of endpoints over their common open; the empty cover fixes the empty value. Extend diagram morphisms by the pushout universal property, proving equivalence with Set-valued forks.

label: prop:fork-total
statement:
\begin{proposition}\label{prop:fork-total}
The categories $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{rec}}$ and
$\mathcal E=\mathcal C_{\mathrm{rec}}^J$ have finite limits and
finite coproducts. The category $\mathcal E$ is regular and
extensive. Its monomorphisms are componentwise injections, and its
regular images are the componentwise c.e.\ images.
\end{proposition}
reconstruction: Regular images and pullbacks are componentwise in the category of c.e. diagrams. Kernel-pair descent is natural by cancellation at the central surjection. Single-element probes at all three positions detect monos. Preimage partition of tagged sums gives extensivity of the diagram category.

label: prop:fork-structure
statement:
\begin{proposition}\label{prop:fork-structure}
The category $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Par}(\mathcal E,
\operatorname{Mono})$ is a split prodominical restriction category
with binary restriction products, restriction coproducts, weak
choice, and ranges satisfying the agreement law. The range of a morphism
represented by $Y\hookleftarrow D\xrightarrow{v}Z$ is the partial
identity on the regular image of $v$.
Joins of restriction idempotents are partial identities on finite
unions of their subfunctors, and inverse image along every partial
morphism preserves binary meets and finite joins. Ranges commute with products and
are stable under pullback along total morphisms.
\end{proposition}
reconstruction: Represent maps by c.e. domain subfunctors and total natural maps on them. Products intersect domains, range uses the componentwise c.e. image, unions give joins, and intersection/union commute with preimages even for partial maps. Inverse search for component injections is natural, yielding weak choice. Restrictions split through their domain and ranges obey agreement and product/base-change laws.

label: prop:fork-local
reconstruction: The subfunctor generated by a central element and its two images is connected, as are one-element endpoint subfunctors. Restrictions to these test both definedness and output at all component elements, proving joint epimorphy of the connected domains.

label: lem:fork-dominance
reconstruction: Embed each component into a number code. At the center retain its own code and the two endpoint codes of its images; endpoint embeddings retain the corresponding code. They form a natural total mono with a computable inverse restricted to its c.e. image.

label: lem:fork-frames
reconstruction: All three required isomorphisms respect transitions. Pair coordinates for products, use parity of the shared first coordinate for sums, and encode a common nonempty word of shared first coordinates with fixed-length codes of the other coordinate sequences for words.

label: thm:fork-turing
statement:
\begin{theorem}\label{thm:fork-turing}
The object $V$ of
$\mathcal A=\operatorname{Par}(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{rec}}^J,
\operatorname{Mono})$ admits a Turing morphism
$\tau:V\times V\rightharpoonup V$: for every object $Y$ of
$\mathcal A$ and every morphism $F:Y\times V\rightharpoonup V$
in $\mathcal A$, there is a total morphism
$p_F:Y\to V$ such that $\tau(p_F\times1_V)=F$.
At component $i\in\{1,2\}$, this Turing morphism is given by
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fork-turing-endpoint}
 \tau_i((k,p),(\ell,x))
 =\operatorname{decode}_2
     \varphi_p(\operatorname{encode}_2(\ell,x)).
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}
reconstruction: Run an ordinary program at each endpoint. At the center run three programs and check agreement of both projected central outputs on their parallel halting domains. For any partial natural family, specialize programs for its exact component domains and form the natural carrier of three indices. With a central input in the original domain the endpoint computations necessarily agree; conversely a returned central value forces its original central domain.

label: prop:fork-recursion
statement:
\begin{proposition}\label{prop:fork-recursion}
Let $\mathscr R_X$ be the full subcategory of $\mathcal A$
whose objects are obtained from $V$ by finitely many applications
of the chosen binary products, binary coproducts, and nonempty-word formation.
Then $\mathscr R_X$ is a recursion category. Its inclusion
into $\mathcal A$ is a range functor, and its restriction
splitting is equivalent to $\mathcal A$.
\end{proposition}
reconstruction: Full subcategory on iterated frame operations is isotypical, prodominical and closed under products/coproducts. The constructed Turing map and parameters belong by fullness. Restriction idempotents, ranges and agreement are inherited. Splitting through their c.e. images gives a fully faithful comparison, and universal embeddings give essential surjectivity.

label: cor:fork-karoubi
reconstruction: For any partial idempotent its c.e. image is in its domain and fixed, hence splits via total inclusion and partial corestriction. Apply this to arbitrary source idempotents: the induced image functor is fully faithful; restriction comparison uses bar f times e. Restriction idempotents already yield essential surjectivity.

label: prop:fork-distinction
reconstruction: Count the five subobjects of the terminal diagram (four with empty center and one with nonempty center), versus two for the numerical singleton. A restriction equivalence would preserve that invariant after completion. Equality on V cannot be decidable because central elements differing only in a discarded coordinate would receive the endpoints' equal answer by naturality.

label: prop:missing-lift
statement:
\begin{proposition}\label{prop:missing-lift}
The category $\mathcal C_K$ is a prodominical recursion category with
binary restriction coproducts and ranges. The functor $F$ is a faithful range functor, preserves restriction products and
reflects zero morphisms, and $F(1_{\N})\ne0$. Inverse images along
total morphisms in its target preserve binary joins of restriction idempotents.
There are a Turing morphism
$\tau_K:\N\times\N\rightharpoonup\N$ and an isomorphism
$b:\N\to\N+\N$ for which the restriction idempotents
\[
 a_0=(b\tau_K\Delta_{\N})^*(1_{\N}+0_{\N}),\qquad
 a_1=(b\tau_K\Delta_{\N})^*(0_{\N}+1_{\N})
\]
are separated by the partial identities on $A$ and $A^c$ for some
nonrecursive set $A\subseteq\N$. Both partial identities belong to
$\mathcal C_K$, and $D_{a_0}\subseteq A$, $D_{a_1}\subseteq A^c$.
There exists a partial function $s:\N\rightharpoonup\N+\N$ with
\[
 s^{-1}(i_0(\N))=A^c,\qquad s^{-1}(i_1(\N))=A.
\]
For every such $s$, there is no morphism
$\ell:\N\rightharpoonup\N+\N$ in $\mathcal C_K$ with $F(\ell)=s$.
Moreover, there are parallel morphisms in $\mathcal C_K$
with disjoint restriction idempotents and no common upper bound in
the restriction order, although finite joins of restriction idempotents
exist.
\end{proposition}
reconstruction: Take the category of ordinary partially recursive extensions with restricted K-c.e. domains. Composition, sums, products, images and joins of domains are realized on their carriers. Uniform specialization of both the ordinary program and the oracle domain index provides a Turing map. The set A of even halting results for the unguarded diagonal is c.e., K-decidable and nonrecursive; it and its complement separate the guarded diagonal. A lift with the prescribed tag preimages would be total, recursive and decide A. The two partial tagged branches even lack a common upper bound.

label: thm:faithful
statement:
\begin{theorem}\label{thm:faithful}
The functor $F_T$ is faithful and preserves restrictions, zeros, binary
restriction products and coproducts, ranges, and finite joins of
restriction idempotents. The category
$\mathcal D_T$ is split and locally connected, satisfies weak choice,
and has inverse images preserving binary joins of restriction
idempotents. Moreover,
$F_T(1_\omega)\ne0$.
\end{theorem}
reconstruction: For every consistent T extending PA, completeness and downward Löwenheim–Skolem give countable countermodels to any unprovable uniform graph identity, taken on carrier ℕ. Their joint graph interpretation is faithful and preserves the operations coordinatewise. Singletons supported at one model witness local connectedness and weak choice of the product and its identity at ω is nonzero.

label: cor:pair
statement:
\begin{corollary}\label{cor:pair}
Let $T\supseteq\PA$ be consistent.
Fix a Turing morphism $\tau:\omega\times\omega\rightharpoonup\omega$ in $S_T$.
Choose an isomorphism $b_0:\omega\to\omega+\omega$ in $S_{\PA}$ and put
$b=\mathsf{quot}_{\PA,T}(b_0)$. Define
\[
 d=\tau\Delta_\omega,\qquad
 a_0=(bd)^*(1_\omega+0_\omega),\qquad a_1=(bd)^*(0_\omega+1_\omega).
\]
Then $a_0,a_1$ are inseparable in $S_T$. For every consistent
extension $T'\supseteq T$, their images under $\mathsf{quot}_{T,T'}$ form the
inseparable pair defined by the same formulas in $S_{T'}$.
\end{corollary}
reconstruction: The quotient S_T→S_T′ is full on program indices, preserves products, total maps and diagonal operations, and carries an arbitrary Turing morphism to one by lifting an arbitrary represented program and then quotienting its source parameter. Apply the source-conditional theorem at a model of each consistent extension.
